name: Hyperbridge HandlerV1 MMR verifier accepts out-of-range leaves
summary: HandlerV1.handlePostRequests copies caller-supplied leaf indices into its inlined MerkleMountainRange verifier, which never rejects leaves outside every peak. A proof with leafCount 1 and a forged leaf at index 1 reconstructs the genuine root from the proof node alone, so the unverified request is dispatched to the host. Forged TokenGateway requests released escrowed WETH, MANTA and CERE and reassigned the bridged-DOT admin, whose unlimited mints were dumped into DOT pools; forged HostManager requests withdrew host fee balances on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum and BNB Chain.
notes: EthereumHost hostParams.handler (slot 15) switched from 0x089248e869aecd66199b64637207d366d6cfe92d to HandlerV1; only the configured handler may call dispatchIncoming.

Floor of exactly measured victim depletion: TokenGateway escrow and host fee balances released by forged requests, plus the counter-assets paid out of pre-existing bridged-DOT pools by swaps before each pool's first liquidity change. Later pool outflows (net 98.05 ETH on Base, 91.12 ETH on Arbitrum over the campaign) mix pre-existing and newly added liquidity and are excluded, as are the dilution of bridged-DOT holders, 14.93 yTRYB, 1527.25 CICADA and 2732.70 faketaxi of unpriced pool outflows, and sub-$20 LINK, VIRTUAL, GMX and EURC outflows. Hyperbridge's revised $2.5m figure includes DOT-denominated losses not measured here. ETH on L2s and native-ETH pools uses the Ethereum WETH price; all prices are taken at the anchor.
